'''Helen Czerski''' (born 1 November 1978{{cn|date=September 2026}}) is a British science writer and broadcaster. She has presented numerous television and radio programmes since 2012, mainly for the [[BBC]], and has written three books and regular columns.

She is Professor of the Environment and Society in the department of [[mechanical engineering]] at [[University College London]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://iris.ucl.ac.uk/iris/browse/profile?upi=HCZER87 |title=Iris View Profile |publisher=Iris.ucl.ac.uk |access-date=2014-06-16}}</ref> She was previously at the [[ISVR#Institute of Sound and Vibration Research|Institute of Sound and Vibration Research]] at the [[University of Southampton]].<ref name="soton">{{cite web|url=http://www.southampton.ac.uk/womensday/helen_czerski.html |title=Dr Helen Czerski :: University of Southampton |publisher=Southampton.ac.uk |access-date=4 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120307020800/http://www.southampton.ac.uk/womensday/helen_czerski.html |archive-date=7 March 2012 }}</ref> Her published research is in the field of [[oceanography]].

==Early life and education==
Czerski was brought up in [[Altrincham]], [[Greater Manchester]], and educated at [[Altrincham Grammar School for Girls]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.messengernewspapers.co.uk/news/9577797.Altrincham_raised_scientist_fronting_major_BBC_series/| title=Altrincham raised scientist fronting major BBC series| first=Rick |last=Bowen| date=8 March 2012|newspaper=[[Messenger Newspapers]]}}</ref> She graduated from the [[University of Cambridge]] where she was a student at [[Churchill College, Cambridge|Churchill College]], with [[Master of Arts]] and [[Master of Science]] degrees in [[Natural Sciences (Cambridge)|Natural Sciences (Physics)]] and a [[PhD]] in experimental explosives physics, particularly [[RDX|Research Department Explosive]] (RDX).<ref name="helenczerski1"/><ref name="czerskiphd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Helen|last=Czerski |title=Ignition of HMX and RDX |publisher=University of Cambridge |date=2006 |url=https://idiscover.lib.cam.ac.uk/permalink/f/16u99e0/44CAM_ALMA21431154150003606|website=cam.ac.uk|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.442574}}|oclc=500335888}}</ref>

==Career==
[[File:Helen Czerski at Thinking Digital 2012.jpg|thumb|Czerski at Thinking Digital in 2012]]
[[File:cmglee Helen Czerski 2013 Cambridge Science Festival.jpg|thumb|upright|Czerski at the 2013 [[Cambridge Science Festival]]]]
Czerski was a regular science presenter for the [[BBC]]. Her programmes<ref name=imdb>{{IMDb name|4937411}}</ref><ref>{{URL|http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p00tvcnx/profiles/helen-czerski|Helen Czerski}} on ''Operation Iceberg'', [[BBC]]</ref><ref>{{URL|http://eden.cms.uktv.co.uk/people/helen-czerski|Helen Czerski}} on Eden</ref> have included:

*''[[Orbit: Earth's Extraordinary Journey]]'', a three-part series on [[BBC Two]], March 2012, co-presented with [[Kate Humble]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b01d7kd5 |title=BBC Two -Orbit: Earth's Extraordinary Journey, Episode 1 |publisher=Bbc.co.uk |access-date=4 March 2012}}</ref>
*''Operation Iceberg'', a two-part series on BBC Two, October 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p00tvcnx|title=BBC Two – Operation Iceberg|work=BBC}}</ref>
*''The Transit of Venus'', BBC Two, June 2012, ''[[Horizon (BBC TV series)|Horizon]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b01jszy4|title=BBC Two – Horizon, 2011–2012, The Transit of Venus|work=BBC}}</ref>
*''Stargazing Challenges'', BBC Two.
*''[[Dara Ó Briain's Science Club]]'', BBC Two.
*''The Secret Life of the Sun'', BBC Two, July 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b03694kd|title=BBC Two – The Secret Life of the Sun|work=BBC}}</ref>
*''Pop! The Science of Bubbles'', [[BBC Four]], April 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.helenczerski.net/broadcast/broadcast.html |title=TV work |publisher=Helen Czerski |access-date=2014-06-16 |archive-date=10 June 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140610022253/http://www.helenczerski.net/broadcast/broadcast.html }}</ref>
*''The £10 Million Challenge'', a ''Horizon'' which launched the [[Longitude Prize 2014]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b044mkxt|title=BBC Two – Horizon, The 拢10 Million Challenge|work=BBC}}</ref>
*''What's Wrong with Our Weather?'', July 2014, ''Horizon'', co-presented with meteorologist [[John Hammond (weather forecaster)|John Hammond]], which examined the possible causes of Britain's recent extreme weather and what connects all the recent extreme winters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b04b763n | title=BBC Two -Horizon: What's Wrong with Our Weather? |publisher=Bbc.co.uk |access-date=17 July 2014}}</ref>
*''Super Senses: The Secret Power of Animals'', August 2014, a three-part series for BBC Two.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/mediacentre/latestnews/2014/new-nhu-series-super-senses|title=BBC – New BBC Two NHU series explores super senses of animal world in Beyond Human – Media centre|work=bbc.co.uk}}</ref>
*''Colour: The Spectrum of Science'', November 2015, a three-part series for [[BBC Four]] on the 15 colours that tell the story of the Earth, life and scientific discovery.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/mediacentre/proginfo/2015/44/colour|title=BBC – Colour: The Spectrum of Science|work=bbc.co.uk}}</ref>
*''Dangerous Earth'', November 2016, a six-part series for the BBC showing how new camera technology is revealing the inner workings of the Earth's most spectacular natural wonders.
*[[The Infinite Monkey Cage]] - ''"[[The Infinite Monkey Cage#Series Fifteen|The Science of Everyday Life]]"'', BBC Radio 4, 16 January 2017.
*''Sound Waves: The Symphony of Physics'', March 2017, a two-part series.
*''From Ice to Fire: The Incredible Science of Temperature'', February 2018, a three-part series.
*''WMG Future Batteries | Fully Charged'', 20 February 2019.<ref>{{cite AV media |date=20 February 2019 |title=WMG (Warwick Manufacturing Group) Future Batteries: Fully Charged |medium=YouTube |language=en |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OlBZ51QLEfs |access-date=25 February 2019 |publisher=fullychargedshow }}</ref>
*''Ocean Autopsy: The Secret Story of Our Seas'', June 2020, a 90-minute film.<ref name="bbc-autopsy">{{cite web |title=Ocean Autopsy: The Secret Story of Our Seas |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m000jy2l#:~:text=Oceanographer%20Dr%20Helen%20Czerski%20and,place%20in%20the%20world's%20oceans.&text=In%20unprecedented%20ways%2C%20humans%20are,seas%20and%20the%20life%20within |publisher=BBC Four |access-date=21 October 2020}}</ref>
*''[[Royal Institution Christmas Lectures]] - Planet Earth: A user's guide'', December 2020, [[BBC Four]] series<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m000qpkf|title=Royal Institution Christmas Lectures|website=bbc.co.uk|access-date=29 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=CHRISTMAS LECTURES 2020: Planet Earth: A user's guide|url=https://www.rigb.org/christmas-lectures/2020-planet-earth-a-users-guide|access-date=2020-08-30|website=www.rigb.org|language=en|archive-date=23 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423083900/https://www.rigb.org/christmas-lectures/2020-planet-earth-a-users-guide}}</ref>

She has also appeared on ''[[The Museum of Curiosity]]'' ([[BBC Radio 4]]) and is an occasional presenter of the web TV and podcast show ''[[Fully Charged]]''. She regularly appears on [[The Cosmic Shambles Network]] and co-hosts their podcasts and web series ''Science Shambles'' and ''They've Made Us'' with [[Robin Ince]]. Until September 2024, Czerski was a regular contributor to the ''[[Wall Street Journal]]'' in the column "Everyday Physics".<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.wsj.com/news/types/everyday-physics| title = Everyday Physics - News, Articles, Biography, Photos - WSJ.com}}</ref> She is the co-host, along with [[Tom Heap]], of ''Rare Earth'', [[BBC Radio 4]]'s premier show on the environment.

=== Awards ===
{{external media | width = 210px | float= right | headerimage= | audio1 = [https://soundcloud.com/user-146467325/podcast-episode-1-dr-helen-czerski-clive-thompson "Episode 1, Dr Helen Czerski & Clive Thompson"], Ada Lovelace Day Podcast | video1 = [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XotBYcft_qQ "Bubble Physicist Helen Czerski"], [[University of Rhode Island]] | video2 = [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DQrbT_BBimA "CS4 Interview: Helen Czerski "], [[University of Southampton]] }}

For her "Everyday Science" column in ''[[BBC Focus]]'' magazine, Czerski was shortlisted for columnist of the year at the 2014 [[PPA Awards]].<ref>{{cite web |date=10 July 2014 |title=PPA Awards 2014 |url=http://www.ppa.co.uk/events/ppaawards2014/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140822130824/http://www.ppa.co.uk/events/ppaawards2014/ |archive-date=22 August 2014 |access-date=21 January 2015 |publisher=[[Professional Publishers Association]] }}</ref> In 2018 Czerski won the [[Kelvin Medal and Prize|William Thomson, Lord Kelvin Medal and Prize]] from the [[Institute of Physics]] for her contributions to championing the physics of everyday life to a worldwide audience of millions through TV programmes, a popular science book, newspaper columns, and public talks.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/page_71751.html|title=IOP Award Winners 2018|last=Physics|first=Institute of|website=www.iop.org|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-07-11}}</ref> Czerski was made an Honorary Fellow of [[Churchill College, Cambridge|Churchill College]], Cambridge in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Helen Czerski |url=https://www.chu.cam.ac.uk/fellows/helen-czerski/ |access-date=2023-08-10 |website=Churchill College |language=en-GB}}</ref> She received an Honorary Doctorate in Science from the [[University of East Anglia]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honorary Graduates - About |url=https://www.uea.ac.uk/web/about/alumni-and-supporters/graduation/honorary-graduates/-/categories/9108888 |access-date=2023-08-10 |website=www.uea.ac.uk}}</ref>

The Italian translation of ''Storm in a Teacup: The Physics of Everyday Life'' won the third edition (2018) of the Premio ASIMOV (Asimov award) for the best book in scientific dissemination published in Italy,<ref>{{cite web |title=HELEN CZERSKI E MARCO MALVALDI VINCONO EX AEQUO IL PREMIO ASIMOV 2018 |url=http://home.infn.it/it/comunicazione/news/2871-helen-czerski-e-marco-malvaldi-vincono-ex-aequo-il-premio-asimov-2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180522111547/http://home.infn.it/it/comunicazione/news/2871-helen-czerski-e-marco-malvaldi-vincono-ex-aequo-il-premio-asimov-2018 |archive-date=22 May 2018}}</ref> and ''Blue Machine: How the Ocean Shapes Our World'' won the 2024 [[Wainwright Prize]] for Writing on Conservation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2024 WINNERS ANNOUNCED |url=https://wainwrightprize.com/news/2024-winners-announced/ |access-date=2024-09-12 |website=Wainwright Prize |language=en-GB}}</ref>
